extraction_note: Explicitly named in README §1's ~9-case carry-forward list, but l4a_axis=alpha_and_gamma (kept as given per instructions) means the alpha component triggers README §1 bullet 2's rescue-recheck instruction, so this is tagged needs_rescue_recheck rather than plain carry_forward. Doc corroborates both components: G1/alpha — correct return value needs two internal getY(...) calls and one getD(...) call chained together, all disallowed inside intentValue; G3/gamma — the intermediate quantities (boundary point M, mid-state xpMid, second invariant d2, partial results y1/y2) exist nowhere in scope, and the doc frames the defect as an intrinsically multi-step sequential chain (M -> y1 -> xpMid -> d2 -> y2) that a single-relation grammar cannot describe as a whole. The doc also notes the boundary point M is itself the root of a nonlinear equation (getD([M,M],a) == d), so even if a call-result reference were allowed, no closed-form value is available — a known-bound rescue is not explicitly tested by the doc for this reason, left flagged rather than re-derived here.
